chunks: And everything in it (the book) that is narrated from Umar ibn Hanzalah, I have transmitted it from Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may Allah be pleased with him - from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Al-Husayn, from Umar ibn Hanzalah.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for narrators
key_terms.صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى: Safwan ibn Yahya, a well-known narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ: Umar ibn Hanzalah, a prominent companion and narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Umar ibn Hanzalah's narrations verified in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous approach to verifying the *isnad* (transmission chain) of narrations attributed to Umar ibn Hanzalah, a key companion of the Imams. By explicitly linking these reports to Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, the author underscores the reliability of the transmission through the prominent Idris family, a lineage highly regarded in Shia hadith scholarship for its precision and piety. This clarification ensures that readers can distinguish between narrations transmitted directly by al-Saduq and those derived from other chains, reinforcing the authenticity of the legal rulings contained within.
